name: sox
desc: SOund eXchange: universal sound sample translator
why: Sox used as an audio instrument and file transformer is a classic Unix sound swiss army knife with many surprising uses.

brief.what_it_is: SoX (Sound eXchange) is a command-line audio utility that converts sound files between formats and can apply effects and filters during the conversion. The SourceForge page describes it as the Swiss Army Knife of sound processing utilities. Its input is audio files in various formats, and its output is converted or processed audio files. Homebrew installs four executables: play, rec, sox and soxi.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no separate rationale beyond the one-line description: it converts audio files to other popular audio file types and applies sound effects and filters during the conversion.
brief.install_notes: The homepage is a SourceForge project page with Windows-oriented download links (sox-14.4.2-win64.exe, sox-14.4.2-win64.zip, sox-14.4.2-win32.zip) and a Download button. User reviews on that page report problems with the Windows installer and with soxi.exe being missing from the distribution. I did not find any Homebrew-specific notes, runtime requirements, or configuration steps on the pages I read.
brief.standout: SoX has been a classic Unix audio tool for decades, and it works as a pipeline utility that can convert, filter and transform sound from a shell. The brew formula's scout notes say it is used as an audio instrument as well as a file transformer, but I did not see examples of that on the pages I read.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The SourceForge page shows a Last Update of 2024-11-28, the project was registered in 2000-09-01, and it has 51 reviews with a 4.7 average. I did not check a commit history or a release page.
brief.caveats: Several user reviews on the SourceForge page report installation trouble on Windows: an installer that runs but leaves no working executable, winget install that does nothing, no default audio device error, and soxi.exe missing. One reviewer says the docs refer to play and rec, which were absent from their download. Another reports that the AD4 format fails with no handler for file extension. These are unverified user reports. The sox.sourceforge.net/sox.html manual URL returned HTTP 404, so I could not read the official manual. The license is GPLv2 or LGPLv2 per the SourceForge listing. The brew caveats field is empty.
quotes: SoX is the Swiss Army Knife of sound processing utilities. It can convert audio files to other popular audio file types and also apply sound effects and filters during the conversion.
The documentation seems to be out of date, referring to Play and Rec which don't come in the download.

judge.reason: SoX is a standout shell-native audio workbench: beyond converting files, it can synthesize sound and compose effects into powerful audio transformations.

entry.title: SoX
entry.tldr: SoX is a command-line audio tool that converts sound files between formats and runs effects and filters on them, all from a shell pipeline.
entry.deeper_look:
SoX, short for Sound eXchange, reads audio in many formats, optionally applies effects and filters, and writes the result in another format. The project describes itself as "the Swiss Army Knife of sound processing utilities." It has been around since 2000 at least, which makes it a long-standing part of the Unix audio toolbox.

Homebrew installs four programs. `sox` does the conversion and processing. `play` and `rec` are shortcuts for playing and recording audio. `soxi` reports information about a sound file. The formula pulls in libraries for FLAC, MP3 (LAME and MAD), Ogg Vorbis, Opus and libsndfile, so a wide range of formats should work after a plain install.

The idea underneath is that audio can be treated like text in a pipeline: a file goes in, a chain of small transformations is applied, and a file comes out. Once sound is something you can filter and rewrite with one command, you can script batch conversions, build test signals, or treat a sound file as raw material for experiments.

The pages the brief draws on gave no usage examples, so the commands below stick to the help output.

entry.whats_unique: SoX combines format conversion and effects in one pipeline-friendly command, and it has been doing so for decades. That makes it a common building block in audio scripts.
entry.caveats: The official manual page returned a 404 when the brief was written, and SourceForge reviewers report install trouble on Windows; the Homebrew build was not tested here.
